German Ambassador Vito Cecere visits Rosenbauer

Top news
News
Vito Cecere, the Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Austria, received a warm welcome in Leonding on August 20. CFO Jörg Schuschnig, CTO Thomas Biringer, and Managing Director of Rosenbauer Deutschland Ronald Reisinger personally accompanied the high-ranking delegation on a tour of Plant 2.
24.08.2026

After the official welcome, Ambassador Cecere was given up-to-date insights into Rosenbauer’s strategic direction and future plans in a company presentation. During the subsequent tour of Plant 2 with a focus on the AT and PANTHER production lines, the diplomatic representative was visibly impressed by the company’s technological competence and innovative strength.

“Rosenbauer International AG is a forward-looking company with close ties to Germany. Impressive technical expertise combined with innovative strength are the hallmarks of this company. I was able to see this firsthand during my visit to the production facility in Leonding.” Vito Cecere, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Austria

“Germany is Rosenbauer’s largest single market in Europe. With more than 600 vehicles sold each year, we are the market leader and continue to see attractive growth potential. In addition to vehicle sales, we are primarily aiming to expand our service business,” said Jörg Schuschnig, CFO of Rosenbauer International AG.  

“To ensure we can continue to provide our customers with the best possible support in the future, we are making targeted investments in the expansion of our sites in Luckenwalde and Bad Abbach. This will strengthen our production and service capacities and lay the foundations for further growth in the German market,” added Thomas Biringer, CTO of Rosenbauer International AG. 

“For Rosenbauer, Germany and Austria are closely connected, and not just because of their geographical proximity. Our locations also work very closely together in development and production. PANTHER is an example of this. The cabins of our internationally successful aircraft rescue firefighting vehicle are manufactured in Luckenwalde and then integrated into vehicle production in Leonding. This close integration is a key strength of our international production network,” said Ronald Reisinger, Managing Director of Rosenbauer Deutschland GmbH.  

 

Germany as the most important single market 

As the largest manufacturer of firefighting vehicles in Germany, Rosenbauer holds a leading position in one of its most important markets. Germany is thus not only a strategic core market but also of central importance for the entire Group. The four locations Luckenwalde, Karlsruhe, Viersen, and Bad Abbach employ a total of around 1,100 people and most recently generated annual revenue of more than €324 million. In addition to the four locations, Rosenbauer has a strong network of mobile service technicians and sales partners who work directly on site with fire departments. 

The Luckenwalde location is the headquarters of Rosenbauer Deutschland GmbH and essential production and service expertise for the German market is brought together here. This is where the Rosenbauer AT, cabins for the PANTHER aircraft rescue firefighting vehicle, and other components for international markets are manufactured. The Group’s largest customer service center is also based in Luckenwalde. With the continuous expansion of the Luckenwalde location and of the Bad Abbach location, which is currently being extended, Rosenbauer is investing strategically in expanding its service capacities in Germany. 

The Karlsruhe location is Rosenbauer’s competence center for aerial rescue vehicles and is one of the leading development and production sites for turntable ladders within the Group. In addition, Karlsruhe has extensive expertise in the refurbishment of aerial rescue vehicles. 

The exchange underscores the strong economic connection between Germany and Austria as well as the importance of cross-location collaboration for the shared success of Rosenbauer.

    Rescue of obese persons
    26. June 2026
    About half of all adults in Germany are overweight, and nearly one in five is considered obese with a body mass index of over 30. Apart from Scandinavia, the situation is similar in many other European countries. For fire brigades and emergency services, these individuals pose a particular challenge during operations. However, thanks to specialized equipment and techniques, even overweight persons can be safely transported using Rosenbauer aerial rescue vehicles.
    News
    Tips
    HEROS H10: One helmet, five certified applications
    26. June 2026
    For a long time, firefighters in German-speaking countries wore the same helmet for all types of operations—whether it was an indoor attack using self-contained breathing apparatus, providing technical assistance after a traffic accident, or fighting a wildfire. However, a shift in thinking has since taken hold in many places, and firefighters are now equipped with two helmets: one for fighting fires inside buildings that offers optimal heat protection, and a lighter one for all other tasks. With the HEROS H10, Rosenbauer offers the ideal helmet for this purpose. It meets five fire service-relevant standards and does not need to be replaced after five years.
